Ryujin Radar's AI Boat Race Predictions

Ryujin Radar is a data analysis site where AI predicts every race held at all 24 boat race venues in Japan, every day. It is completely free, with no sign-up required.

For every race we lay out each racer's win rate, average start timing and results by course, motor performance, and wind and wave data. You can also check, from actual past results, how races under matching conditions were decided.

In Ryujin Sonar, you can check the results of past races under close conditions, and the past rates when you change the entry or start pattern.

Once you open a race, check it with these

Ryujin Sonar

The "Ryujin Sonar" tab on the race page

How were past races with this line-up decided?
If boat 1 can't escape, which boats tend to come in?
Pick a venue racing today from the list above
Press "View details" on a race
Open the "Ryujin Sonar" tab
Pick a venue racing today ↑

📝 Boat Race Strategy Blog

Prediction tips, venue guides, and data analysis to boost your win rate

🌟 Featured Articles
Data Analysis
What Is Winning-Technique Analysis? A New Way to See Win Patterns by Venue and Lane

A new feature analyzing which winning technique (wire-to-wire, inside pass, outside overtake, etc.) led to 1st place, broken down by venue and lane, using 90 days of race data. Learn how to use it as evidence for picks or exclusions.

7 min
Data Analysis
What Is Motor Condition? A New Way to See Today's 2nd-Place Rate by Lane

A new feature showing each boat's motor 2nd- and 3rd-place rate for today's races, just by selecting the race. Designed to be directly usable for real betting decisions, not just an abstract motor ranking.

7 min
Data Analysis
Does Boat Racing AI Prediction Really Hit? — Results from 3 Months and 15,000 Races

We audited AI prediction hit rate and return rate across 15,000 races. An honest look at its strengths and weaknesses, how Ryujin Radar differs from other services, and where AI prediction falls short.

10 min
🆕 New Articles
Beginner
The Beginner's Guide to Getting Started with Boat Racing — From Buying a Ticket to Using AI Predictions

A complete guide for anyone wanting to start boat racing — basic rules, all 7 bet types explained, how to register for TELEBOAT, beginner-friendly betting approaches, and how to think about your budget.

10 min
How-To
What Are First-Mark Turn Predictions? How AI Reads the Way a Race Unfolds

A full breakdown of Ryujin Radar's turn prediction feature — how it statistically forecasts the first-mark turn from each racer's winning-technique distribution, ST, and motor performance, and how to use it in your betting strategy.

10 min
Beginner
The Complete Guide to Predicting Boat Races — Raise Your Hit Rate with Data and AI

The 6 key factors in boat race prediction, explained with data from over 10,000 races. A beginner-friendly guide to reading racer win rate, motors, lanes, ST, exhibition runs, and weather — plus how to use AI prediction.

Can I see the AI boat race predictions for free?Ryujin Radar's AI predictions are free, with no sign-up required. The past rates in Ryujin Sonar can also be checked without signing up.
What data can I check when looking at the AI predictions?In Ryujin Sonar, you can check the results of past races under close conditions and the past rates for each entry or start pattern. The race card also shows racer and motor records.
In what order should I read Ryujin Sonar?Check the date, venue, race number and race card first, then read the conditions, period and number of races in Ryujin Sonar.
Can I use it before the exhibition?Before the exhibition, you can still check the race card records and past race tendencies. Exhibition times and other same-day values appear after the exhibition, so "preparing" or "—" until then does not mean zero.
Are the past rates the predicted probability for this race?The past rates are the results of past races under the conditions you chose on screen, not the predicted probability for this race. Read them together with the conditions, period, number of races, and how finishing order and refunds are handled, and do not use them as a guaranteed number.
